body: Wixom Industrial One, LLC filed suit against the City of Wixom on August 7, 2026 in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan, alleging the city violated the state's zoning act, WHMI reported, citing Crain's Detroit. The complaint seeks declaratory judgment, injunctive relief and damages, according to the court docket (No. 2:26-cv-12754, assigned to Judge Robert J. White).

The property is 54 acres on South Wixom Road north of Interstate 96, assembled for an industrial park by the company's developer according to WHMI. After Missouri real estate firm Sansone Group approached the developer, the site was pitched for a data center. Exhibits to the complaint identify the site as 30625 S. Wixom Road and include a city email stating that the parcel is zoned M-1, Light Industrial. The city adopted a six-month moratorium on data center development after public sentiment shifted, and in July the City Council rejected a proposed waiver from it.

The developer alleges the city used its rough site plan for a three-building, 519,400-square-foot campus to write ordinances that would effectively bar data center development on property zoned for it, and it describes itself as the victim of a council more concerned with public opinion than with the law, according to WHMI. The article did not include a response from the city. The docket shows the city filed a motion to dismiss on September 1, Wixom Industrial One filed an amended complaint on October 6, the city filed another motion to dismiss on October 20, and the developer responded on November 10.

timeline.label: Wixom City Council rejects a proposed waiver from its data center moratorium
Wixom Industrial One files suit in the Eastern District of Michigan
Wixom Industrial One files an amended complaint after the city's first motion to dismiss
Wixom Industrial One responds to the city's October 20 motion to dismiss
